items.abstract: <jats:p>For the OEIS sequence A348410, counting integer-distribution arrays via a(n) = <a rel="nofollow">x^n</a>^(-n), R. J. Mathar (19 October 2021) and V. Kotesovec (1 November 2021) each contributed to the OEIS entry a conjectured P-recursive recurrence for a(n) — Mathar's of order 4, Kotesovec's of order 2 — neither of which has been proven. Building on T. Niu's recent derivation of the explicit algebraic equation P(t,A)=0 satisfied by the ordinary generating function A(t)=∑a(n)t^n [Niu 2026], we carry the derivation the rest of the way: we extract from P(t,A)=0 an order-4 linear ODE for A(t) and the corresponding order-4 recurrence for a(n), verify it as an exact power-series identity, and show by exact polynomial (shift-operator) division that this recurrence, and independently Mathar's conjectured recurrence, both factor exactly as left-multiples of Kotesovec's order-2 recurrence. Combined with a short induction argument seeded by verified base cases, this proves Kotesovec's conjecture unconditionally, with Mathar's conjecture following as an immediate corollary.</jats:p>
title: A Proof of Kotesovec's and Mathar's 2021 Recurrence Conjectures for OEIS A348410

items.abstract: <jats:p>For the OEIS sequence A177265 (the number of permutations of {1,. .. , n} having exactly one string of consecutive fixed points), R. J. Mathar contributed on 1 July 2022 the conjectured order-4 P-recursive recurrence a(n)-(n-1)a(n-1)-(n-1)a(n-2) + (n-1)a(n-3) + (n-2)a(n-4) = 0, n ≥ 5, which has remained unproven on the OEIS entry. We prove it. In fact we show something stronger: a(n) satisfies the previously unrecorded order-3 recurrence (n-1) a(n)-(n2-n1) a(n-1)-n a(n-2) + n(n-1) a(n-3) = 0, n ≥ 4, and that Mathar's order-4 recurrence is an immediate algebraic consequence of this order-3 recurrence: it equals the sum of the order-3 recurrence evaluated at n and at n-1, divided by (n-1). The order-3 recurrence is derived directly from the combinatorial definition of a(n) together with the classical derangement recurrence D(n) = n D(n-1) + (-1)ⁿ; the proof is entirely self-contained and relies on no unproved OEIS comment.</jats:p>
title: A Short Proof of Mathar’s 2022 Recurrence Conjecture for Oeis A177265, via a new Order-3 Recurrence

items.abstract: <jats:p>On May 7, 2024, R. J. Mathar contributed to OEIS A186185 a conjectured order-6 Precursive recurrence, with a matching asymptotic conjectured the same day by V. Kotesovec. We give a short proof, deriving an explicit cubic algebraic equation for the generating function from its defining functional equation and extracting the recurrence via the Bostan-Chyzak-Salvy algebraic-to-holonomic correspondence.</jats:p>
title: A Proof of Mathar's Recurrence Conjecture for OEIS A186185

items.abstract: <jats:p>The empirical managerial accounting literature has failed to produce a substantive cumulative body of knowledge. This literature has not matured beyond describing practice to developing and testing theories explaining observed practice, like other areas of accounting research. While the lack of publicly available data is a popular reason for this literature's underdeveloped state, it is not the only one. Other conjectures include: its inductive approach, researchers' incentives, its use of non-economics-based frameworks, the lack of empirically testable theories, and its emphasis on decision making, not control.</jats:p>
title: Conjectures Regarding Empirical Managerial Accounting Research

items.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>In this short paper we establish identities involving sums of products of binomial coefficients and coefficients that satisfy the general second–order linear recurrence. We obtain generalizations of identities of Carlitz, Prodinger and Haukkanen.</jats:p>
title: On Binomial Sums for the General Second Order Linear Recurrence
